title: PennyLane Finance - Embedding + Rerank Hosting Evaluation
summary: Discovery with PennyLane Finance to understand embedding/rerank needs for a consumer fintech search and inbox assistant. Key concerns: throughput for peak trading hours, vector DB integration, hybrid search (BM25 + emb), hosting choices (hosted vs dedicated vs private/VPC), encryption/KMS, and cost tradeoffs. Agreed next steps: share security pack, run 2-week pilot with 50k vectors, provide benchmark matrix and pricing for hosted vs dedicated, schedule technical deep dive for infra team.
action_items: Samira Khan: Send security whitepaper + SOC2 attestation (due: 2025-10-15)
Ethan Park: Attach benchmark template and ask for sample traffic profile (due: 2025-10-14)

next_steps: Redwood to send hosted vs dedicated pricing comparison and expected qps per instance

transcript:
Header:
Date: 2025-10-12
Start time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~46 minutes
Attendees: Samira Khan (Redwood AE), Ethan Park (Redwood SE), Maya Lopez (PennyLane Head of Search), Ravi Desai (Infra), Jen Park (ML Eng), Connor Hill (PM)

[00:00] Samira Khan: Hi everyone, thanks for taking the time. I'm Samira from Redwood, and I'm joined by Ethan, our solutions engineer. How's everyone doing?
[00:12] Maya Lopez: Hey Samira, hi Ethan, good thanks. We're excited to talk embeddings and rerank — been trying to tame search latency at peak.
[00:18] Ethan Park: Great. Quick agenda: learn about your current stack, constraints, and success metrics; discuss hosting options — hosted, dedicated, private/VPC; then talk about embedding dims, vector DBs, and a pilot. Sound ok?
[00:27] Connor Hill: Sounds good. I'll try to keep time.
[00:30] Maya: Quick context — PennyLane is consumer fintech, 3M MAU, search for support inbox and transaction lookup. Peak concurrency around market open and close, we see spikes in embed+rerank traffic.
[00:42] Jen Park: Our current pipeline: we embed with an open model in-house, store vectors in a managed vector DB (we're on Chroma for dev), and do a two-stage: approximate search then a small transformer reranker hosted on EC2. It's getting expensive and p95 is creeping up.
[00:59] Ravi Desai: From infra side, we're sensitive to network egress and want to avoid wide open data flows. We have a VPC and want KMS integration for any keys. SOC2 is required and we have compliance folks to involve.
[01:12] Ethan: Totally — those are common. Quick question on scale: what's the average qps for search and what are your tail latency targets for rerank?
[01:20] Maya: Average is ~120 qps for search, but spikes up to 1.2k qps for short bursts, hence our interest in dedicated capacity. For UX we want p95 under 300ms for the first-pass retrieval and p95 under 700ms end-to-end including rerank.
[01:36] Samira: Thanks. So three buckets to consider: cost vs latency vs operational complexity. Redwood Hosted gives faster time-to-value, automatic batching and prefix cache, but dedicated gives predictable throughput for spikes, and Private/VPC gives you the control you need for keys/audit.
[01:51] Jen: Do you recommend storing vectors in our existing vector DB or using Redwood's embedding storage? We want to avoid re-architecting too much.
[02:00] Ethan: Both are supported. We often see customers use hybrid — Redwood serves embeddings and rerank, but vectors live in your DB (Pinecone/Chroma/Milvus/Qdrant). Redwood can do a fallback path: first-pass search in your vector DB, then call Redwood reranker with candidate docs. That avoids moving the whole corpus.
[02:17] Connor: Any perf hit with that hop?
[02:19] Ethan: There's network overhead; typical extra 20–50ms if both services are in same cloud region and you have good peering. If you want absolute minimum latency, colocating reranker and vector store in same VPC or using Redwood Dedicated in the same region reduces that overhead.
[02:34] Maya: We care about cost too. How does quantization or dim reduction affect rerank quality? We're currently at 1024 dims for some datasets but would consider 768 or 512.
[02:44] Ethan: Lower dims cut storage and search time but may slightly harm recall depending on content. For financial text short notes, 768 often hits the sweet spot. For rerank you can keep a smaller candidate set (top 100) from the vector DB at 512 or 768 and let a cross-encoder reranker on Redwood score the final top 10. That preserves final quality while reducing cost.
[03:03] Jen: Are there Redwood-verified profiles for embed dims/throughput so we can compare?
[03:07] Samira: Yes, we'll share our performance matrix and recommended quantization profiles per model and dims. Ethan will attach a benchmark template.
[03:14] [03:15] Maya: On hosting — if we go Redwood Private or Dedicated, what network constructs do we need? VPC peering? Transit gateway?
[03:21] Ethan: For Private, you get a customer-managed control plane and we do VPC peering or private link depending on your cloud. For Dedicated, you can have reserved GPU pools in our infra with VPC peering to your network. Both support KMS/HSM integrations for encryption at rest. We also provide audit logs for compliance.
[03:35] Ravi: Important — our compliance team will ask for key rotation policy and whether Redwood stores any unencrypted data.
[03:42] Samira: We’ll include KMS details and our encryption at rest policy in the security pack. You can have keys in your KMS for Private deployments. For Hosted we offer managed keys but can do customer-managed keys for enterprise.
[03:54] Connor: About reranker cost — if we run cross-encoders on Redwood, what's typical tokens per call and cost per query?
[04:01] Ethan: Depends on prompt size and docs length. For a 512-dim embedding rerank with top 10 docs, cost is mainly compute; we'll give a sample pricing line item. Also batching and continuous KV cache for chat scenarios can reduce token cost.
[04:14] Maya: How does Redwood handle fallbacks during capacity constraints? For example, if dedicated pool saturated during market open spike.
[04:20] Samira: We offer routing policies and automatic fallback to compatible model variants or hosted spare capacity. You can set SLOs to prefer latency or cost. For critical flows you can provision burst capacity.
[04:33] Jen: We're interested in a short pilot. We'd like to run a two-week pilot with about 50k vectors and traffic profile matching peak windows. What's a minimal setup to prove p95 and econ?
[04:43] Ethan: Minimal pilot: Redwood Hosted or Dedicated sandbox, ingest 50k vectors into your DB (or we can ingest a mirrored index), build hybrid search path to call your vector DB for top-k, call Redwood reranker for top-10. We'll record p95 retrieval and p95 end-to-end as well as cost per q. We can run parallel tests for hosted and dedicated to compare.
[04:58] Maya: Good. Any blockers for data residency? We need data to stay in us-east-1 for now.
[05:04] Samira: We support region pinning. For Private, obviously stays in your environment. For Dedicated we can pin the pool to us-east-1. Hosted also allows region choice when supported.
[05:13] Ravi: Network question — will we need to open inbound from Redwood IP ranges? We usually avoid whitelisting external IPs.
[05:19] Ethan: For VPC peering or Private link you don't need public IPs; for hosted you may need controlled egress to Redwood endpoints, or use an SSM-like connector. We can detail the network flow in the next doc.
[05:29] Maya: Any known gotchas integrating with Qdrant/Chroma? We saw some customers hit vector mismatch due to normalization differences.
[05:36] Ethan: Yep. Normalization, metric (cosine vs euclidean), and embedding scaler differences matter. We'll share a checklist: ensure embeddings use same preproc, consistent L2 norm if using cosine, and test recall on small slices.
[05:47] Connor: Who are your recommended partners for vector DB migrations?
[05:50] Samira: We have partners and an integration guide. For migrations our solutions team can assist with an ETL that keeps doc ids so reranker calls map cleanly.
[05:59] Jen: For the pilot, we'd like Redwood to run a side-by-side: our current reranker on EC2 vs Redwood reranker, same data and traffic. Is that doable?
[06:06] Ethan: Absolutely. We'll instrument the test with the benchmark template and measure p50/p95/p99 and cost. We'll need your anonymized dataset and representative request traces.
[06:15] [06:30] Maya: Anything you want from us right now?
[06:32] Samira: If you can share the anonymized sample dataset and a short traffic profile (qps per minute across a day), we'll get a scoped pilot plan and costs. Ethan will send the benchmark template.
[06:43] Ravi: We'll check with security before sending data. We'll probably require an NDA but we got a standard pilot NDA.
[06:49] Samira: Fine. We can sign the pilot NDA. We'll also include a draft statement of work for the 2-week pilot.
[06:55] Connor: Timeline? If we start docs this week can we spin up pilot next week?
[07:00] Samira: We can aim for kickoff on 10/20 if paperwork and sample data are ready.
[07:05] Maya: One more technical — how do you handle KV cache for rerank/recall across sessions? We have some conversational flows where a user's previous queries should bias retrieval.
[07:14] Ethan: Redwood runtime supports KV cache and prefix caching; for retrieval you can pass session context or embeddings of recent messages to bias the search. We also support local caching layers to keep hot vectors collocated.
[07:26] Jen: We saw reference to quantized embeddings; do you do product-level quantization or rely on DB-level compression?
[07:32] Ethan: Both. We provide quantization-friendly profiles that work with int8/4 quantization on the model side and vector DBs often offer compressed indexes. We'll experiment in the pilot with 8-bit quantized embeddings and 768 dims to balance cost and accuracy.
[07:44] Maya: Excellent. Anything else on security or legal we should flag?
[07:48] Ravi: Data retention for logs and audit — we need 12 months of audit logs.
[07:52] Samira: We can configure retention in the console and support exporting logs to your SIEM. We'll include details in the security pack.
[07:59] Connor: Ok sounds like a plan.
[08:02] Samira: Recap of next steps: Redwood sends security pack + SOC2, attach benchmark template and pricing matrix, PennyLane to share NDA and anonymized sample, schedule infra deep dive.
[08:13] Ethan: I'll follow up with the benchmark sheet and a recommended minimal pilot config: hosted vs dedicated compare, 50k vectors, top-k=100, rerank top10.
[08:22] Maya: Thanks everyone, appreciate the clarity.
[08:26] Ravi: Thanks. We'll loop in compliance and get the NDA signed.
[08:30] Samira: Great. We'll send the materials by 10/15 and propose deep dive slots. Thanks all.

End of transcript.
